name: Chest-Supported Row (Alternating Arms)
description: The alternating chest-supported row performs each arm separately on an incline bench, allowing the non-working arm to hold at peak contraction while the other arm descends and returns. This creates a unique combination of isometric and dynamic loading within a single set, increasing total upper back time under tension while maintaining strict torso support.

execution.starting_position: Lie prone on an incline bench set to 30-45 degrees. Hold a dumbbell in each hand, arms hanging down.
execution.setup_instructions: Set the incline bench so that the chest is fully supported throughout the movement. Use a weight that allows clean alternating reps.
steps: Step 1: Row both dumbbells to the top position simultaneously to start.
Step 2: Hold the left dumbbell at peak contraction.
Step 3: Lower the right dumbbell to full extension while holding the left.
Step 4: Row the right dumbbell back to the top.
Step 5: Hold right at top; lower left; repeat the alternating pattern.
execution.breathing_instructions: Breathe continuously — do not hold breath for the entire set.
common_mistakes: Not actually holding at peak — both arms should not move simultaneously
Losing scapular retraction during the hold phase
safety_considerations: The chest-supported position eliminates lower back stress — suitable for lower back pain sufferers
Keep the head in a neutral position — do not crane the neck
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full arm extension to elbows behind torso on each arm.
coaching_cues: One arm holds while the other works
Keep both shoulder blades retracted throughout
